approaches.title: Per-bit counting modulo three
approaches.summary: Counts occurrences of each bit position across all numbers, then reconstructs the value from bit counts modulo three.

Simplified bit extraction with shifts and replaced reverse reconstruction with direct indexed bit placement.

approaches.title: Bitwise finite-state counters
approaches.summary: Tracks each bit’s occurrence count using two bit masks representing the one-occurrence and two-occurrence states. XOR and masking cycle each bit through counts zero, one, two, and back to zero.

revisions.commitBody:
Just think about counting each bit, and abstract away thinking about the
actual number

ones and twos act as counting buckets for each bit position.
They record whether each bit has occurred once or twice.
If trice, wrap back to 0 and don't count.

ones = (ones ^ n) & !twos:
XOR toggles bits in ones, counting them. However, bits already present
in twos are masked out, because their count is advancing from two to
zero.

twos = (twos ^ n) & !ones:
XOR toggles bits in twos. Bits currently present in ones are masked out,
because their count is advancing from zero to one.

Thus each bit cycles through zero, one, two, zero occurrences, and the
bits remaining in ones represent the number that occurred once.
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaced the per-bit counting array with constant-space `ones` and `twos` bitwise state masks.
